title: Git: Working Tree, Changes, Commits
learningObjectives: Inspect status to see changed and untracked files.
Stage only files intended for the snapshot.

understand.concept: Git separates current working-tree edits, staged changes prepared for the next commit, and recorded commits. The staging area lets you choose which changes belong in the next snapshot. A commit records staged content and metadata, not every unsaved or unstaged edit.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear, repeatable practices help beginners make safe changes and understand how work moves from an idea to a checked result.
understand.analogy: A small checklist helps a person complete a task in order without forgetting important steps.
understand.analogyLimit: Software workflows also involve technical tools, dependencies, collaboration, and test evidence, which a checklist analogy cannot fully describe.

explain.narrative: A safe routine is to inspect status, review diffs, stage only intended files, commit with a clear message, then inspect status and history again. If unrelated edits exist, leave them unstaged or handle them separately.
